reading.a: A white sun stands high in a red-orange evening sky over a dark city of tall blocks on the left bank of a river, with a white fountain plume on the right, and its orange reflection runs straight down the middle of the dark rippled water.
reading.b: A white sun sits on top of a thin chimney just above a low industrial skyline of cranes, pylons and stacks, in a golden sky under a wide dark cloud bank with thin lit streaks, and its gold reflection runs straight down the blue-grey water.

concepts.idea: One sunset becomes the other inside one frame (3.0 s): the camera tilts up and draws back slightly, so the sun travels from row 225 down to row 459 and the waterline goes with it from row 545 to about row 731 (B's is at 736), while B's cloud bank comes in from the top as the camera's own surround; the red sky turns gold from the first frame (t 0-0.6, 0-1.8 s), the tall city on the left bank folds down into the low port with its cranes and the chimney (t 0.10-0.80, 0.3-2.4 s), the sun settles onto B's sun on the chimney by centre and shape and mixes into it limb first (t 0.25-1.0, 0.75-3.0 s), and what remains of A's sky and water closes in a circle around the sun (t 0.20-0.90) before the last of A gives way brightest-first (t 0.86-1.0, 2.6-3.0 s).

anchors.how: Sun on sun. Measured by the planner on the two canvases: A's bright disc is centred at (940.9, 224.8) with radius 39.0 px (the luma falls from 240 at 38 px to 162 at 45 px, so min_L 220 keeps the orange glow, about 160, out of the fit; round 11's 120 would take it in); B's bright disc at frac 0.9 is centred at (962.3, 459.3) with radius 33.2 px (frac 0.8 takes in B's glow, 195-211, and returns a 78 px disc at (960, 439)). The camera's scale 0.85 = 33.2 / 39.0 also carries A's waterline (row 545) to about row 731 against B's 736, so one similarity aligns the sun and the horizon.

A's dark city band (the blocks, the shoreline trees, the banks and the embankment wall, rows 93-679) against B's dark industrial band (the skyline with cranes and pylons, the chimney under the sun, the stacks, the far bridge and the near bank, rows 300-797). A's bridge (17, its matte keeps about half of its mask) and the fountain (10, bright) are left in A's base on purpose.

transforms.name: red_sky_to_gold
transforms.note: The lead, not a beat: A's red sky and water move in Lab statistics toward B's golden sky, its glow and its sea from the first frame, so the radial key from t 0.2 crosses two fields that are already close in colour.

transforms.name: city_folds_into_port
transforms.note: Beat 1, a band onto a band (the kind he liked on the bridge into the arm): the tall blocks on the left bank lower and spread into the low port, and the cranes, pylons and the chimney under the sun are delivered inside the moving matte. No rate is named: nothing in the pair asks for a fast or a slow fold, so the concept's smooth trapezoid holds. Guarded: B's skyline, chimney included, cannot show before this beat delivers it.

transforms.name: sun_onto_sun
transforms.note: Beat 2, the last, ending at the last frame. The two suns have nearly the same size in the frame once the camera's 0.85 scale applies (39.0 x 0.85 = 33.2 px), so this recede shrinks the disc very little; its work is rule 4: end_shape b_blob moves the disc onto B's bright blob by centroid, axes and angle, and the late mix dissolves it into that blob limb first. blob_frac 0.9 instead of the default 0.6, because at 0.6 of the local maximum (about 151) B's glow (195-211) joins the blob. Profile linear and no rate: a sun onto a sun of the same size asks for no fast shrink. reveal_ahead true is the recede's default, written out; the vacated ring is about one pixel wide here.

knobs.name: pullback.params.end_scale
knobs.what: The camera's end scale; 0.85 lands the sun on the sun by radius and the waterline within 5 rows of B's, smaller pulls back further and drops A's waterline above B's.

knobs.name: container.params.sky.radial_near_at
knobs.what: When the radial window around the sun reaches A's top edge (the nearest edge, about 297 rows above the sun in the re-cropped A); earlier removes A's straight top edge sooner as B's cloud bank comes in, later keeps A's red sky above the sun longer.

knobs.name: sun_onto_sun.params.blob_frac
knobs.what: Which of B's bright blobs the sun ends on; 0.85 already takes in part of the glow (a 54 px disc), 0.9 and 0.95 give the 32-33 px disc.

concepts.risk: Rule 1: B's cloud bank (rows 0-207) and two side strips (columns 0-162 and 1794-1919) show from the first frames as the camera's surround; that is the declared early region of a disc container, but nothing else of B should appear before its beat, so read b_inside_first and look at the chimney under the sun at t 0.2-0.5. Rule 5: until the radial window reaches A's top edge (radial_near_at 0.2) the top of A's frame is a straight horizontal edge moving down over the red sky; read residual_edge_max at t 0.05-0.25. Rule 7: the sky key over t 0.2-0.9 is a luma crossfade of sky into sky and water into water inside a shrinking circle; the colour lead makes the two fields close, but he has called every reveal a crossfade, so this is where the concept is weakest. Rule 2: the camera's move is short (scale 1 to 0.85, about 234 px of travel at the sun), so the first and last tenths of the clip may read as still; read motion_pauses. Rule 4: B's chimney touches the bottom of B's sun (its top at row 489 against the disc's bottom at 492); if the blob search takes in the chimney's lit edge the oval tilts; read end_blob. F3 invention: none; every pixel comes from A or B.
